new_gain.name: finite multiband critical endpoint gluing
new_gain.statement: For dyadic spectral projections P_j and J_j=E int ||P_jY||^3, ||T_TY||_{Z_{3,2/3}} <= 65 sqrt(66) (sum_j J_j^(2/3))^(1/2) whenever the right side is finite. In particular, if Y is supported in N arbitrary dyadic blocks, the norm is <529 N^(1/6)||Y||_3; for two arbitrary dyadic blocks it is <594||Y||_3, independent of their spectral separation.
new_gain.mechanism: dimension-free 2-convex square-function inequality for Z_{3,2/3}, combined with the predecessor 65 sqrt(2) dyadic-block endpoint
new_gain.source_level_change: none; unrestricted full-spectrum endpoint remains open
new_gain.quantitative_improvement: For finite spectral ratio K, an alternative bound <529(2+ceil(log_2 K))^(1/6), improving the predecessor 65 sqrt(K) loss for sufficiently wide ranges.

essential_dependencies: P24 exact endpoint r_*=3 and endpoint failure
failed_or_insufficient_route: Black-box block endpoint gluing alone still leaves the factor (sum J_j^(2/3))^(1/2); arbitrary L^3 input only controls sum J_j. Thus this mechanism cannot by itself close the unrestricted full-spectrum endpoint.
residual_obstruction: Remove the N^(1/6)/spectral-cubic-entropy loss for arbitrarily many simultaneously active dyadic bands by exploiting common-Brownian cross-scale covariance/Hellinger structure, not only separate block bounds.
next_attack: Prove a covariance-improved 3-convex/Carleson gluing inequality for active dyadic bands; two arbitrarily separated active bands are now already controlled at the critical 2/3 exponent.
